source_text: Ἠλίας ἅρμα πυρὸς καὶ ἵππους πυρίνους πρὸς αὐ τὸν ἐλθόντας οὐ κατεπλάγη, ἀλλ' ἐπιθυμίᾳ τῆς ἄνω πορείας τῶν φοβερῶν κατετόλμησε, καὶ μετὰ περιχαρείας ἐπέβη τῶν φλογίνων ὀχημάτων, ὁ ἐν σαρκὶ ζῶν ἔτι· σὺ δὲ, οὐ πυρίνων ἁρμάτων ἐπιβήσεσθαι μέλλων, ἀλλὰ δι' ὕδατος καὶ Πνεύματος ἀνα βαίνειν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, οὐκ ἐπιτρέχεις τῇ κλήσει; Ἔδειξεν Ἠλίας τοῦ βαπτίσματος τὴν ἰσχὺν ἐπὶ τοῦ βωμοῦ τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων, οὐ διὰ πυρὸς, ἀλλὰ δι' ὕδατος τὴν θυσίαν ὁλοκαυτώσας. Ἄλλως μὲν οὖν ἡ τοῦ πυρὸς φύσις τῷ ὕδατι μάχεται· ἐπειδὴ δὲ μυ στικῶς τὸ ὕδωρ τρίτον τότε τοῦ βωμοῦ κατεχύθη, ἀρχὴ ἐγένετο τῷ πυρὶ, καὶ ἐξῆψε τὴν φλόγα ὥσπερ ἔλαιον. Λάβετέ μοι, φησὶν, ὑδρίας, καὶ ἐπιχέετε ἐπὶ τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς σχίδακας. Καὶ εἶπε· Δευτερώσατε, καὶ ἐδευτέρωσαν· Τρισσώσατε, καὶ ἐτρίσσωσαν δεικνύντος τοῦ λόγου, ὅτι διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος τῷ Θεῷ οἰκειοῦται ὁ προσ αγόμενος, καὶ ὅτι φῶς καθαρὸν καὶ οὐράνιον ἐν ταῖς τῶν προσιόντων ψυχαῖς διὰ τῆς εἰς τὴν Τριάδα πίστεως ἀναλάμπει. Εἰ χρυσὸν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ διένεμον, οὐκ ἄν μοι εἶπες· Αὔριον ἥξω, καὶ αὔριον δώ σεις· ἀλλ' ἀπῄτεις ἂν ἤδη τὴν διανομὴν κατεπείγων, καὶ ἐδυσφόρεις πρὸς τὴν ὑπέρθεσιν· ἐπειδὴ δὲ οὐχ ὕλης εὔχροιαν, ἀλλὰ ψυχῆς καθαρότητα προτεί νεταί σοι ὁ μεγαλόδωρος, προφάσεις πλάττῃ καὶ αἰ τίας ἀπαριθμῇ, δέον ἐπιτρέχειν τῷ δώρῳ. Ὢ τοῦ θαύ ματος! ἀνακαινίζῃ, μὴ χωνευόμενος· ἀναπλάττῃ, μὴ συντριβόμενος· θεραπεύῃ, μὴ ὀδυνώμενος, καὶ οὐ λογίζῃ τὴν χάριν. Εἰ δοῦλος ἀνθρώπων ἦσθα, προ εγράφη δὲ δούλοις ἐλευθερία, οὐκ ἂν ἐπὶ τὴν κυρίαν ἀπήντησας, συνηγόρους μισθούμενος, καὶ δικαστὰς παρακαλῶν, ὥστε πάσῃ μηχανῇ πρὸς ἐλευθερίαν ἐξαιρεθῆναι; Ἤ που καὶ ῥάπισμα, τὴν τελευταίαν τῶν δούλων πληγὴν, ὑπὲρ τῆς μετὰ ταῦτα τῶν αἰκισμῶν ἀπαλλαγῆς κατεδέχου. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ δοῦλον ὄντα σε, οὐκ ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, καλεῖ πρὸς ἐλευθερίαν ὁ κῆρυξ, ἵνα λύσῃ μέν σε τῆς αἰχμαλω σίας, ἰσοπολίτην δὲ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις ποιήσῃ, καὶ υἱὸν μὲν ἀποδείξῃ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσποιηθέντα διὰ τῆς χάριτος, κληρονόμον δὲ τῶν ἀγαθῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ· οὔπω λέγεις εἶναί σοι καιρὸν δέξασθαι τὰ διδόμενα. Ὢ τῶν πονηρῶν ἐμποδίων! ὢ τῆς αἰσχρᾶς καὶ ἀτελέστου ἀσχολίας! Ἕως πότε ἡδοναί; ἕως πότε ἡδυπάθειαι; Πολὺν ἐζήσαμεν χρόνον τῷ κόσμῳ, ζήσωμεν λοιπὸν καὶ ἑαυτοῖς. Τί ψυχῆς ἀντάξιον; Τί ἰσοστάσιον τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν; Τίς ἀξιοπιστότερός σοι σύμ βουλος τοῦ Θεοῦ; Τίς φρονιμώτερος τοῦ σοφοῦ; ἢ τίς ὠφελιμώτερος τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ; Τίς τοῦ κτίσαντος οἰκειότερος; Οὐδὲ τῇ Εὔᾳ συνήνεγκε τῇ τοῦ ὄφεως συμβουλῇ πεισθῆναι μᾶλλον ἢ τῇ τοῦ Δεσπότου. Ὢ τῆς ἀτοπίας τῶν λόγων! Οὐκ ἄγω σχολὴν ὑγιᾶναι· μήπω μοι δείξῃς τὸ φῶς· μήπω συνάψῃς τῷ Βασιλεῖ. Οὐ ταῦτα λέγεις ἄντικρυς; Μᾶλλον δὲ τὰ τούτων ἀλογιστότερα. Σὺ δὲ, εἰ μὲν ἦς ἐγγεγραμμένος τοῖς δημοσίοις ὀφλήμασι, χρεῶν δὲ ἀποκοπαὶ τοῖς ὑπευθύ νοις περιηγγέλθησαν, εἶτά τις ἦν ὁ πρὸς ἐπήρειαν ἄμοιρόν σε ποιῆσαι τῆς συγχωρήσεως ταύτης ἐπιχει ρῶν· ἠγανάκτεις ἂν καὶ ἐβόας, ὡς τὸ ἐπιβάλλον σοι μέρος τῆς κοινῆς χάριτος ἀφαιρούμενος.
thought_title: Elijah's water kindles fire; grace offered, excuses made
orientation: Basil is still addressing those who delay baptism, now using Elijah's water-drenched sacrifice as a figure of baptism's power and then confronting the hearer's excuses directly.
pass_a_gloss: Elijah was not terrified at a chariot of fire and fiery horses coming toward him, but with desire for the upward journey he dared the fearful things, and with great joy he mounted the flaming vehicles, while still living in flesh; but you, who are about to mount not fiery chariots, but through water and Spirit to go up into heaven, do you not run to the call? Elijah showed the power of baptism upon the altar of the whole burnt offerings, not through fire but through water consuming the sacrifice as a whole burnt offering. In one way then the nature of fire fights against water; but since mystically the water was poured upon the altar a third time then, it became a beginning for the fire, and it kindled the flame just like oil. Take for me, he says, water jars, and pour upon the whole burnt offering and upon the wood. And he said: Do it a second time, and they did it a second time; Do it a third time, and they did it a third time, the word showing that through baptism the one being brought near is made a member of God's household, and that pure and heavenly light shines forth in the souls of those who approach through faith in the Trinity. If I were distributing gold to the church, you would not have said to me: Tomorrow I will come, and tomorrow you will give; but you would have demanded the distribution already, urging it on, and you would have been annoyed at the delay; but since not the fine color of matter, but purity of soul is offered to you by the great giver, you fabricate pretexts and count up excuses, when you ought to run to the gift. O the wonder! You are renewed, without being melted down; you are remolded, without being crushed; you are healed, without being pained, and you do not reckon the grace. If you were a slave of men, and freedom had been proclaimed for slaves, would you not have gone to meet the lady, hiring advocates and entreating judges, so that by every device you might be rescued for freedom? Surely you would even have accepted a slap, the last blow of slaves, for the sake of release from the tortures after these things. But since you are a slave, not of men, but of sin, the herald calls you to freedom, in order that he may release you from captivity, and make you a fellow citizen with the angels, and show you as a son of God adopted through grace, and an heir of the good things of Christ; you still say that it is not yet the time for you to receive what is being given. O the wicked obstacles! O the shameful and endless busyness! How long pleasures? How long luxuries? We have lived a long time for the world; let us live henceforth also for ourselves. What is worth a soul? What is equal in weight to the kingdom of heaven? Who is a more trustworthy counselor to you than God? Who is wiser than the wise one? Or who is more beneficial than the good one? Who is more intimate than the creator? It did not benefit Eve to be persuaded by the counsel of the serpent rather than by that of the Master. O the absurdity of the words! I have no leisure to be made well; do not yet show me the light; do not yet unite me to the King. Do you not say these things outright? Or rather things more irrational than these. But you, if you had been enrolled in the public debts, and cancellations of debts had been announced to those liable, and then someone was attempting through malice to make you have no share in this pardon; you would have been indignant and would have cried out, as one being robbed of the portion of the common grace that falls to you.

lemmas.gloss: is made a member of the household

choices.english: is made a member of God's household
choices.why: The verb means to be brought into a familial or intimate relationship; 'member of God's household' captures the domestic sense Basil is building toward adoption.
The compound means 'great-gifted' or 'giving great gifts'; rendering as a noun phrase keeps the epithet's force without a hyphenated compound.

choices.english: You are renewed, without being melted down
choices.why: The passive participles describe what is not done to the person; keeping them as separate clauses preserves the contrast Basil draws between baptism and metalworking.
rejected: you are being renewed, not melted

choices.why: κυρία is the feminine of κύριος, here meaning the mistress or lady who grants freedom; 'the lady' keeps the social setting of manumission.

choices.english: make you a fellow citizen with the angels
choices.why: ἰσοπολίτης means one having equal civic rights; 'fellow citizen with the angels' preserves the political metaphor Basil uses for heavenly citizenship.
rejected: an equal citizen with the angels

choices.why: The word denotes soft or luxurious living; 'luxuries' keeps the plural exclamation parallel with 'pleasures'.

bible_refs.note: Λάβετέ μοι ὑδρίας, καὶ ἐπιχέετε ἐπὶ τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς σχίδακας. Καὶ εἶπε· Δευτερώσατε... Τρισσώσατε

pass_b_english: Elijah was not terrified when a chariot of fire and horses of fire came to him; he longed for the journey upward, and so he dared those fearful things. With great joy he mounted the flaming vehicle while still living in the flesh. But you are not about to mount a chariot of fire; you are about to ascend to heaven through water and the Spirit—and you do not run to the call? Elijah showed the power of baptism at the altar of whole burnt offerings, when he consumed the sacrifice not with fire but with water. By nature fire and water are at war with each other, but when the water was mystically poured over the altar a third time, it became the starting point for the fire and kindled the flame as if it were oil. “Take jars,” he says, “and pour water on the whole burnt offering and on the pieces of wood.” And he said, “Do it a second time,” and they did it a second time. “Do it a third time,” and they did it a third time (1 Kings 18:33-34). The word shows that through baptism the one who comes forward is made a member of God's household, and that pure, heavenly light shines forth in the souls of those who approach through faith in the Trinity. If I were distributing gold to the church, you would not say to me, “I will come tomorrow, and tomorrow you will give it.” You would demand the distribution at once, pressing me, and you would be annoyed at any delay. But since the great giver is offering you not the fine color of matter but the purity of your soul, you invent pretexts and count up excuses when you ought to run to the gift. What a wonder! You are renewed, without being melted down; you are reshaped, without being broken; you are healed, without suffering pain—and you do not reckon the grace. If you were a slave of human beings, and freedom had been proclaimed for slaves, would you not have gone to meet the lady, hiring advocates and pleading with judges, so that by every means you might be delivered into freedom? Surely you would even have accepted a slap on the face—the last blow a slave receives—to be rid of the abuses that would follow. But now you are a slave, not of human beings, but of sin, and the herald calls you to freedom, to release you from captivity, to make you a fellow citizen with the angels, to show you as a son of God adopted through grace, and an heir of the good things of Christ—and you still say it is not yet the time for you to receive what is being given. What wicked obstacles! What shameful, endless busyness! How long will pleasures last? How long will luxuries last? We have lived a long time for the world; let us live from now on for ourselves. What is worth as much as the soul? What weighs equally with the kingdom of heaven? Who is a more trustworthy counselor to you than God? Who is wiser than the wise one? Who is more helpful than the good one? Who is closer to you than the Creator? It did not benefit Eve to obey the serpent's counsel rather than the Master's. What absurd words! “I have no leisure to be made well; do not show me the light yet; do not unite me to the King yet.” Is this not what you are saying outright? Or rather, things even more irrational than these. If your name had been written in the public debt records, and a cancellation of debts had been announced to those who owed, and then someone tried out of malice to keep you from sharing in that pardon, you would be outraged and you would cry out that he was robbing you of your portion of the common grace.

last_rejected.quote: What a wonder! You are renewed, without being melted down; you are reshaped, without being broken; you are healed, without suffering pain—and you do not reckon the grace.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὢ τοῦ θαύ ματος! ἀνακαινίζῃ, μὴ χωνευόμενος· ἀναπλάττῃ, μὴ συντριβόμενος· θεραπεύῃ, μὴ ὀδυνώμενος, καὶ οὐ λογίζῃ τὴν χάριν.
last_rejected.why: Source has 'you do not reckon the grace' as a direct question; English drops the interrogative force, making it a flat statement.
last_rejected.fix: —and do you not reckon the grace?
last_rejected.ruling: καὶ οὐ λογίζῃ τὴν χάριν is a statement with interrogative force implied by context, not a direct question; English captures the rhetorical rebuke adequately.

last_rejected.quote: to show you as a son of God adopted through grace
last_rejected.source_quote: υἱὸν μὲν ἀποδείξῃ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσποιηθέντα διὰ τῆς χάριτος
last_rejected.why: εἰσποιηθέντα means 'adopted'; 'adopted through grace' is redundant and slightly distorts the construction.
last_rejected.fix: to show you adopted as a son of God through grace
last_rejected.ruling: εἰσποιηθέντα means 'adopted as a son'; 'adopted through grace' renders διὰ τῆς χάριτος accurately, not redundant.
